affected.help:
Usage: repo-contract affected [options]

Show which tests and mutation targets the changes in the working tree can affect, compared
with a base commit. When the analysis cannot be sure, it says so and reports everything.

Options:
  --base <ref>   Compare against <ref> (default: the upstream branch, then origin/main,
                 then origin/master)
  --tsconfig <file>
                 Read module-resolution options (paths, baseUrl) from <file> instead of
                 tsconfig.json
  -C <dir>       Run as if started in <dir>
  --json         Print a machine-readable report (schemaVersion 1)
  --explain      Say why each test is affected
  --tests        Print only the affected test files, one per line
  --sources      Print only the affected source files, one per line
  --mutate       Print only the mutation targets, one per line
  --shard <i>/<n>
                 Keep only shard <i> of <n> of the mutation targets, balanced by
                 recorded time (with --timings) so the shards finish together
  --timings <file>
                 JSON object of file to milliseconds, used to balance shards
  --plan-shards  Print a GitHub Actions matrix (JSON) for the mutation targets;
                 needs --shards or --target-minutes
  --shards <n>   --plan-shards: use <n> shards (never more than there are targets)
  --target-minutes <n>
                 --plan-shards: size the shards to about <n> minutes each
  --max-shards <n>
                 --plan-shards: with --target-minutes, use at most <n> shards
  -h, --help     Show this help
  -V, --version  Print the version

Exit status: 0 on success (even when everything is affected), 1 if the command could not
run, 2 for a usage error.

cache.help:
Usage: repo-contract cache <command> [options]

Inspect and tidy the computation cache (default: .repo-contract/cache).

Commands:
  stats          Count the entries, their size and the unreadable ones, per check
  clear          Remove every entry
  prune          Remove unreadable entries, and any beyond the limits below
  why <check> --inputs <file>
                 Say how <check>'s current inputs (a JSON object of input name to
                 digest) differ from its latest cache entry

Options:
  -C <dir>             Run as if started in <dir>
  --cache-dir <dir>    Use <dir> as the cache (default: .repo-contract/cache)
  --json               Print a machine-readable report (schemaVersion 1)
  --max-age <n>d|<n>h  prune: remove entries older than this
  --max-entries <n>    prune: keep only the <n> newest entries
  --inputs <file>      why: JSON object of input name to content digest
  -h, --help           Show this help
  -V, --version        Print the version

Exit status: 0 on success, 1 if the command could not run, 2 for a usage error.

doctor.help:
Usage: repo-contract doctor [options]

Look for settings that make affected-scope runs slower or wrong, and say how to fix each. Examples
are a cache directory that is not ignored, a shallow CI checkout, and a coverage config without the
json reporter. Nothing is changed unless you pass --fix, which applies only the safe, mechanical repairs
and shows each change first.

Options:
  --fix          Apply the safe repairs
  --json         Print a machine-readable report (schemaVersion 1)
  -C <dir>       Run as if started in <dir>
  -h, --help     Show this help
  -V, --version  Print the version

Exit status: 0 on success (even when there are findings), 1 if the command could not run,
2 for a usage error.

init.help:
Usage: repo-contract init

Scaffolds repo-contract.config.mts and scripts/contract.mjs from your package.json's declared
dependencies, and wires "scripts.contract" into package.json. That is all this command does.
Checks always run afterwards via `npm run contract`, never through this CLI.

merge-mutation.help:
Usage: repo-contract merge-mutation --total <n> [options] <shard>=<file>...

Combine the mutation reports of the shards of one run (see 'repo-contract affected --shard') into
one report. Name each report with its shard number, so a shard that never reported is noticed:

  repo-contract merge-mutation --total 3 --out reports/mutation.json 1=s1.json 2=s2.json 3=s3.json

Options:
  --total <n>   How many shards the run was split into (required)
  --out <file>  Write the merged report to <file> instead of stdout
  -C <dir>      Run as if started in <dir>
  -h, --help    Show this help
  -V, --version Print the version

Exit status: 0 on success, 1 if the shards cannot be merged, 2 for a usage error.

metrics.help:
Usage: repo-contract metrics [options]

Summarize the run log: pass rate, failures by check and pillar, cache hit ratio, how much of the
test suite affected runs needed, estimated minutes saved, first-pass rate and the mutation score
trend. Only what the log supports is shown.

Options:
  --log <file>     Read <file> (default: .repo-contract/metrics/runs.jsonl)
  --since <when>   Only runs since a date (2026-11-01), or within the last <n>d or <n>h
  --actor <who>    Only runs by 'human' or 'agent'
  -C <dir>         Run as if started in <dir>
  --json           Print a machine-readable report (schemaVersion 1)
  -h, --help       Show this help
  -V, --version    Print the version

Exit status: 0 on success, 1 if the command could not run, 2 for a usage error.

repo-contract.help:
Usage: repo-contract <command> [options]

Commands:
  repo-contract init            Scaffold repo-contract.config.mts and scripts/contract.mjs
  repo-contract affected        Show which tests and mutation targets the current changes can affect
  repo-contract merge-mutation  Combine the mutation reports of a sharded run (fails if a shard is missing)
  repo-contract metrics         Summarize the run log: pass rate, cache hits, time saved, failures by check
  repo-contract doctor          Find settings that slow or break affected-scope runs, and fix the safe ones
  repo-contract cache           Inspect and tidy the computation cache (stats, clear, prune, why)

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help
  -V, --version  Print the version

Run 'repo-contract <command> --help' for more on a command. Checks themselves run via
`npm run contract`, never through this CLI.

CheckEvidence.description:
What actually happened when one configured check ran. `output` is present only if that check's config requested a format, and is otherwise `undefined`: a policy narrows with `ctx.result.output?.success` (or an `if (ctx.result.output) { ... }` guard) before reading `.value`/`.error`.

`output.value` is the value the configured `format` parser produced. If the check's config supplies `output.schema` (see `CheckDefinitionConfig.output.schema`), the schema validates it and may replace it with a transformed value, so it is not always the raw parser result.

It is typed `unknown` for every format, including `"text"` (where `parseText` always produces a `string`), with or without a schema. TypeScript's generic inference cannot carry one check's literal `output.format`, or its schema's output type, through to that check's `policy` once several checks with different formats share one `checks` record. That limit was confirmed during implementation; specs/decisions/ holds the isolated repro. This is a deliberate tradeoff. A schema still types its author's own code through `StandardSchemaV1<Input, Output>`, but not this shared `CheckEvidence` shape. A policy author narrows or casts `.value`, as they already must for `"json"` or `"text"` without a schema.

args.description: The arguments passed to `command`, exactly as spawned.

command.description: The executable that was actually spawned (after tokenization, if `run` was a string).

completedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the process reached its terminal state.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time from spawn to termination, in milliseconds.

exitCode.description: `null` when the process never exited normally: see `signal` and `status`.

output.description: The parsed interpretation of `stdout`, present only if this check's config requested a `format`. If that config also supplied `output.schema`, a successful parse is additionally validated (and possibly transformed) by that schema before landing here: see this interface's own doc comment above and `CheckDefinitionConfig.output.schema`.

signal.description: The signal that terminated the process, if any. `null` for a normal exit or a spawn failure.

skipReason.description: Present only when the check never spawned because the run opted in to fail-fast (`RunRepoContractOptions.failFast`) and a cheaper check had already failed (see `CheckDefinitionConfig.expensive`). Such a check has `status: "aborted"`: it did not run, so a policy must never read it as a pass.

spawnError.description: Populated only for `status === "spawn_error"`: the underlying Node error message (e.g. "spawn foo ENOENT"). Never populated for any other status.

spawnErrorCode.description: Populated only for `status === "spawn_error"`: the underlying Node `ErrnoException`'s structured `.code` (e.g. `"ENOENT"`, `"EACCES"`), when Node provides one. Never populated for any other status. Distinguishes "the executable does not exist" from other spawn failures (permission denied, invalid executable format, etc.) without parsing `spawnError`'s free-text message.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the process was spawned.

status.description: Why the process reached its terminal state; see `CheckStatus`.

stderr.description: The process's raw standard error, captured verbatim up to an internal size cap (10 MiB); content beyond the cap is replaced with a truncation marker.

stdout.description: The process's raw standard output, captured verbatim up to an internal size cap (10 MiB); content beyond the cap is replaced with a truncation marker.

CheckStatus.description:
Why a check's process ended up in its terminal state. `"completed"` means the process ran to exit on its own: the exit code may still be non-zero, and that is for the check's policy to interpret, never this package. The other five values all mean the process did not exit on its own; repo-contract terminated it, or it was terminated for a reason repo-contract can observe but did not cause.

`"signaled"` specifically means a signal repo-contract did *not* itself request: an externally-caused termination. A check is instead `"host_terminated"` when the *host* process running repo-contract received its own SIGINT/SIGTERM (see `run-checks.ts`'s termination-handler cleanup). In that case repo-contract did request the signal, though not via `options.signal` or `timeoutMs` (see `"aborted"`/`"timed_out"`). So it must not be conflated with an externally-caused `"signaled"`.

Evidence.description: Versioned, immutable record of one complete `runRepoContract` execution: every configured check's evidence, plus timing for the run as a whole. Says nothing about whether any of it was acceptable; see `Verdict`. Adding, removing or changing a direct member of this interface requires bumping `version`. This repository's `api-contract` check fails the change otherwise. It does not compare the members of `CheckEvidence`, so changes there are held to the rule in `VERSIONING.md` by review only.

checks.description: Each configured check's own evidence, keyed by check id.

completedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the last check finished.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time for the run as a whole, in milliseconds.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the run began.

version.description: Schema version of this shape; see `VERSIONING.md`.

OutputFormat.description: Output interpretation a check can explicitly request. No format requested means no parsing: the consumer gets raw stdout/stderr only. Other formats (e.g. YAML) are left out on purpose: JSON and plain text cover every check this package or its consumers run. A check whose tool emits another format converts it in its own `run` step, or reads it in its `policy` function with a library it already depends on. That keeps this package free of an optional peer dependency carried on everyone's behalf.

ParsedOutput<unknown>.description: The result of a check's requested output-format parse: either a successful `ParsedOutputSuccess`, or a `ParsedOutputFailure`.

ParsedOutputFailure.description: A requested parse of a check's stdout failed. The raw stdout on the parent `CheckEvidence` is preserved unchanged: a parse failure is never silently reinterpreted or discarded.

format.description: The format that was requested (and failed to parse).

ParsedOutputSuccess<unknown>.description: A requested parse of a check's stdout succeeded.

format.description: The format that was requested and successfully parsed.

./schema.description: Machine-readable record of what happened when a repo-contract configuration was executed. It has one entry per configured check, describing the command run, its exit status, captured output, and (if requested) parsed output. Says nothing about whether the result was acceptable; the paired Verdict schema says that. Generated from src/types.ts's Evidence type, never hand-authored.
./schema.title: repo-contract Evidence

It has one entry per configured check, describing the command run, its exit status, captured output, and (if requested) parsed output. Says nothing about whether the result was acceptable; the paired Verdict schema says that. Generated from src/types.ts's Evidence type, never hand-authored.
./schema/evidence.title: repo-contract Evidence

PolicyOutcome.description: `"pass"`: the repository-owned policy evaluated the captured evidence as satisfying its configured requirements. `"fail"`: the evidence did not satisfy them. `"warn"`: the evidence does not violate the policy's blocking requirements, but the policy decided the condition matters and wants it surfaced. It is not a synonym for "minor failure". A `warn` never fails `Verdict.passed` (see `runPolicies` in `src/policy/run-policies.ts`).

PolicyResult.description:
A repository-owned policy's interpretation of one check's captured evidence. It is a plain object of primitives, never an `Error`, class instance, function or tool-specific object. So it can be persisted, transmitted, aggregated across parallel checks, and read by a human or an AI without rerunning anything.

`rationale` is mandatory. It must hold enough actionable detail (specific file/line locations, rule ids, test names, counts) for a consumer to understand *why* the policy reached its outcome from this value alone. A rationale like "see output above" or "check the report for details" defeats the purpose: it sends the consumer back to raw command output, which this type exists to avoid. `runPolicies` rejects such a rationale at runtime (`src/policy/run-policies.ts`'s `VAGUE_RATIONALE_PATTERNS`, ADR 0016), the same as any other malformed `PolicyResult`. So a check that regresses to a vague deferral fails loudly instead of shipping silently. specs/architecture.md describes the split this type is built around. Evidence answers "what happened?". `rationale` answers "what does the repository's policy conclude about what happened?". A policy's `outcome` is not the final word: a human or AI consumer still judges using both.

rationale.description: Why the policy reached `outcome`, in enough detail to act on without rerunning anything.

Verdict.description: Versioned, immutable aggregate result of evaluating every configured check's policy against its evidence: each check's own `PolicyResult`, verbatim, keyed by check id. `passed` is `true` only if every check's `outcome` is `"pass"` or `"warn"`: `"fail"` is the only outcome that fails the run; one failing check never collapses into a single generic message, every check remains individually inspectable under `checks`. Versioned independently of `Evidence` (see `VERSIONING.md`'s schema-versioning policy): `version: 2` reflects `checks[id]` changing shape from `{ passed, reason? }` to a full `PolicyResult` (`{ outcome, rationale }`); see ADR 0001.

checks.description: Each configured check's own `PolicyResult`, verbatim, keyed by check id.

passed.description: `true` only if every check's `outcome` is `"pass"` or `"warn"`.

version.description: Schema version of this shape; see `VERSIONING.md`.

./schema/verdict.description: Machine-readable aggregate pass/fail result produced by evaluating repository-owned policies against an Evidence object. It has one entry per configured check, each individually inspectable. Generated from src/types.ts's Verdict type, never hand-authored.
./schema/verdict.title: repo-contract Verdict
